# `b10x-loom`

Generated from the clap definition of the `b10x-loom` command line in [`crates/loom-cli/src/lib.rs`](https://github.com/beyond10x/loom/blob/main/crates/loom-cli/src/lib.rs) by `loom-docs`. It lists only commands that exist.

> Loom: route an intent and run it until it is blocked

`b10x-loom --version` prints its version, and `--help` after any command prints the text below.

## Commands

| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| [`b10x-loom run`](#b10x-loom-run) | Run the slice on an intent until it is blocked, and say why it stopped |
| [`b10x-loom protocols`](#b10x-loom-protocols) | Install, inspect, or remove protocol definitions available to this host |
| [`b10x-loom protocols add`](#b10x-loom-protocols-add) | Validate and snapshot one protocol from a file or a pinned Git repository |
| [`b10x-loom protocols list`](#b10x-loom-protocols-list) | List bundled and installed definitions, provenance, and available execution bindings |
| [`b10x-loom protocols remove`](#b10x-loom-protocols-remove) | Remove an installed definition; bundled definitions cannot be removed |
| [`b10x-loom evaluate`](#b10x-loom-evaluate) | Decide a case snapshot and its evidence under a catalog protocol, and write the decision as JSON. It decides and never acts |
| [`b10x-loom plugin`](#b10x-loom-plugin) | Host a plugin, or print what it proposed. A plugin reads and proposes; it never sends |
| [`b10x-loom plugin run`](#b10x-loom-plugin-run) | Host a plugin: poll, classify and answer each new item in a governed read-only turn, and record one line per handled item. Nothing is sent |
| [`b10x-loom plugin report`](#b10x-loom-plugin-report) | Print one line per proposal a plugin recorded in its state directory: a proposed reply or a proposed case |
| [`b10x-loom approve`](#b10x-loom-approve) | Approve the request a commission's Suspension holds: write a grant into the state directory. Approval performs nothing; `resume` does |
| [`b10x-loom resume`](#b10x-loom-resume) | Continue a commission's suspended run after its approval: perform the suspended request once, release the Suspension, and run on until the run stops |

## `b10x-loom run`

Run the slice on an intent until it is blocked, and say why it stopped

```text
Usage: b10x-loom run [OPTIONS] <INTENT>
```

| Argument | Required | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--context-policy <CONTEXT_POLICY>` | no | `legacy` | Keep the legacy rolling transcript, or opt into bounded working context and history lookup |
| `--context-report <PATH>` | no | none | Write payload-free measurements, including routing and startup failures |
| `--confinement <CONFINEMENT>` | no | `substrate` | Confine tests with Substrate, or explicitly run with the operator's rights |
| `--cgroup-root <DIR>` | no | none | An explicitly delegated cgroup v2 root for confined tests |
| `--workspace <DIR>` | no | none | Existing Git worktree for software changes; unnecessary for system queries |
| `--test-cmd <CMD>` | no | `cargo test` | The test command, run in the workspace without a shell: a program and its arguments, split at white space |
| `--max-steps <N>` | no | `20` | The most actions performed before the run stops |
| `--catalog <PATH>` | no | none | An llm catalog (`llm.catalog/1` TOML) in a regular file; a named pipe such as `<(cmd)`, a device or a directory is refused. With it, `--model` and `--classifier-model` each name a route alias of this catalog instead of a Codex model, both of them; an alias it does not declare, or a catalog that cannot be read, stops the run before any model call |
| `--config <PATH>` | no | none | A models configuration (YAML, a regular file): `routes`, the path of an `llm.routes/1` document relative to the configuration's directory, and `roles`, a list of `{role, model}` giving the roles `agent` and `classifier` each a route or `<endpoint>/<model-id>` name of that document, whose credentials are its `secret:` references. With it, `--model` and `--classifier-model` have no default: given, each overrides its role with a name of the same document. A configuration that cannot be loaded, a role neither configured nor given, or a model that cannot take a forced tool call stops the run before any model call. Not with `--catalog`, nor with `--state`: a resume context keeps no configuration |
| `--model <ID>` | no | `gpt-5.6-sol` | The model that selects actions and writes their arguments: a Codex model name, with `--catalog` a route alias of that catalog, or with `--config` a name of its routes document, overriding the role `agent` |
| `--classifier-model <ID>` | no | `gpt-5.6-sol` | The model that classifies the intent: a Codex model name, with `--catalog` a route alias of that catalog, or with `--config` a name of its routes document, overriding the role `classifier` |
| `--threshold <X>` | no | `0.5` | The confidence, from 0 to 1, below which the router refuses its pick |
| `--risk <RISK>` | no | `standard` | How much proof the change must carry, the software-change@1 case input `risk`: each level owes every obligation of the level below it and one more (tests, review, provenance, health). A protocol that declares no case input ignores it |
| `--change-kind <KIND>` | no | `feature` | What the change is, the software-change@1 case input `change_kind`. A bugfix edits the implementation (implementation.edit) only once a test failed on the current revision |
| `--affects-security-boundary <BOOL>` | no | `false` | Whether the change affects a security boundary, the software-change@1 case input `affects_security_boundary`. One that does is verified only once another principal approved its security review, which the slice never submits |
| `--test-path <GLOB>` | no | none | A test-path pattern, repeatable: tests.write changes only paths one of them matches, for every change kind; a path outside them refuses the action before anything is written. Relative to the workspace root; `*` within one path segment, `**` across any number. Without one: tests/**, **/tests/**, test/**, **/test/**, **/*_test.*, **/test_*.*, **/*.test.* and **/*.spec.* |
| `--regression-test-command <CMD>` | no | none | The regression-test command, run in the workspace without a shell and split at white space, with {path} in at least one word. On a bugfix, after each tests.run that follows a tests.write that committed, it runs once per test path those writes committed, {path} filled, and only its result is a regression_test_result. Without it no run is one, so a bugfix's red_first.required stays open |
| `--output <FORMAT>` | no | `human` | What standard output carries: lines for a person, or one JSON record per line, the last one the terminal record with the stop reason and the exit status |
| `--state <DIR>` | no | none | Keep the run's case, its commission's Suspension and the commission's resume context in this directory, created when missing, so a run stopped for an approval leaves what a later resume continues from. Without it nothing outlives the run |
| `--action-bindings <FILE>` | no | none | A run configuration file (JSON, a regular file) binding an installed protocol's actions to commands: {"protocol": "<name>@<major>", "timeout_seconds": <n>, "unconfined_bindings": <true\|false>, "bindings": [{"action": "<action>", "argv": ["<program>", "<argument>", ...]}]}. A run of that protocol starts an admitted action's program without a shell, with the action's arguments as JSON on standard input, a cleared environment but PATH, and a timeout (60 s when absent); exit 0 is performed, with standard output, one JSON object, as the report; any other end is refused. A binding confers no authority. A file that names an action the protocol does not declare is refused before any model call; an action it binds no command to stops the run NoLocalExecutor, naming it. Substrate does not confine these commands, so the run is refused ConfinementUnavailable (CommandUnconfined), exit 3, before any model call unless --unconfined-bindings is given or the file sets "unconfined_bindings": true |
| `--unconfined-bindings` | no | `false` | Run the commands --action-bindings binds with the operator's rights, outside Substrate. Without it, and without "unconfined_bindings": true in that file, a run given --action-bindings is refused ConfinementUnavailable (CommandUnconfined). The flag wins over the file; standard error reports which one opted in |
| `<INTENT>` | yes | none | What to do, as given |

```text
With --state, only a run whose last line is `stopped: ApprovalRequired (<action>)` holds a
Suspension `approve` can approve.

Exit status:
  0  the query completed (Completed) or the run reached its human gate (ApprovalRequired)
  4  with --state, the run reached its human gate holding no Suspension:
     `stopped: ApprovalRequired (<action>), nothing suspended`; there is nothing to approve
  3  the run stopped for another reason (NothingAdmissible, StepBudget, NoLocalExecutor, Refused, ConfinementUnavailable)
  1  the run failed
  2  the command line is not valid
```

## `b10x-loom evaluate`

Decide a case snapshot and its evidence under a catalog protocol, and write the decision as JSON. It decides and never acts

```text
Usage: b10x-loom evaluate [OPTIONS]
```

| Argument | Required | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `--input <PATH>` | no | none | Read the request from this regular file instead of standard input; a named pipe, a device or a directory is refused (pipe a request to standard input instead) |

```text
The request is one JSON object (loom.evaluation.EvaluationRequest):
  {"protocol": "<name>@<major>", "snapshot": {canon-case/1}, "evidence": [{canon-evidence/1}, ...], "at": "<RFC 3339>",
   "decisions": [{"decision": "<name>", "outcome": "<outcome>", "principal": "<who>", "case_revision": "<revision>"}, ...]}
`at` and `decisions` are optional. The protocol comes from this host's catalog (`protocols list`), never from the request.
`decisions` are the canon-decisions/1 explicit decisions taken for the case; one applies only at the snapshot's revision.
A record that is not a readable canon-evidence/1 record, or repeats an earlier record's id, is refused.
A readable record that does not apply to the case (an undeclared kind or subject, for instance) is set
aside, as the governor sets it aside, and the decision is made from the rest without listing it.
Unlike the governor, which sets an unreadable record and a repeated id aside (keeping the first) and
still decides, evaluate refuses both (a repeated id as duplicate-identifier, naming the later record).

Exit status:
  0  decided: standard output carries the decision (loom.evaluation.EvaluationDecision)
  3  refused: standard output carries the refusal (loom.evaluation.EvaluationRefusal), and standard error names the input
  1  the request or the protocol catalog cannot be read
  2  the command line is not valid
```

## `b10x-loom plugin run`

Host a plugin: poll, classify and answer each new item in a governed read-only turn, and record one line per handled item. Nothing is sent

```text
Usage: b10x-loom plugin run [OPTIONS] --config <PATH> --state <DIR> <PLUGIN>
```

| Argument | Required | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `<PLUGIN>` | yes | none | The plugin to host |
| `--config <PATH>` | yes | none | The plugin's JSON configuration file |
| `--state <DIR>` | yes | none | The plugin's state directory: its cursors and record. It must lie outside every workspace root and checkout the configuration names; one host holds it at a time |
| `--once` | no | `false` | Run one cycle and stop |
| `--catalog <PATH>` | no | none | An llm catalog (`llm.catalog/1` TOML) in a regular file. With it, `--model` and `--classifier-model` each name a route alias of this catalog instead of a Codex model; an alias it does not declare, or a catalog that cannot be read, stops before any model call |
| `--model <ID>` | no | `gpt-5.6-sol` | The model each turn runs on: a Codex model name, or with `--catalog` a route alias |
| `--classifier-model <ID>` | no | `gpt-5.6-sol` | The model that classifies each item and picks a task's protocol: a Codex model name, or with `--catalog` a route alias |

```text
The configuration is the plugin's JSON configuration file. For slack-handler it is
loom.slack.SlackConfig: the host's plugin configuration under "plugin" (the connectors command line,
the data sources a turn may read, the objectives, the classification threshold, the poll interval),
the Slack adapter, connection and read operations, the bot's user id, min_age_minutes, the seed,
lookback_minutes and the objectives each channel serves. It is checked before anything runs.

Each cycle polls, classifies every new item, answers a question in a governed read-only turn over the
data sources and records the proposed reply, records a task's proposed case, and appends one line per
handled item to record.jsonl in the state directory. Nothing is sent. With --once it runs one cycle
and prints one line per proposal it recorded. Without it, it polls every poll_interval_seconds until
SIGTERM or SIGINT, which end it after the item being handled (a second one ends it at once, exit
status 130), and then prints one line per proposal it recorded.

Exit status:
  0  the cycles ran
  1  the configuration, the models or the state directory cannot be used, or the last cycle's poll
     failed (a failed poll is otherwise retried after poll_interval_seconds)
  2  the command line is not valid (an unknown plugin name among them)
  130  a second SIGTERM or SIGINT ended it at once
```

## `b10x-loom approve`

Approve the request a commission's Suspension holds: write a grant into the state directory. Approval performs nothing; `resume` does

```text
Usage: b10x-loom approve [OPTIONS] --state <DIR> <COMMISSION> <CAPABILITY>
```

| Argument | Required | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `<COMMISSION>` | yes | none | The commission whose Suspension is approved: the id its resume context and Suspension carry |
| `<CAPABILITY>` | yes | none | The capability approved; it must be the one the suspended request needs |
| `--state <DIR>` | yes | none | The state directory `run --state` kept the commission in. It must exist |
| `--mandate <FILE>` | no | none | The host-trusted Mandate file (loom.authority.MandateHost): also record a Mandate approval of the request, by the file's approver, in the state directory's approval log; the grant names it, and `resume --mandate` clears it through Mandate |

```text
Approval performs nothing. It reads the commission's Suspension in the state directory and
writes a grant (intake.routing.Grant) for the one request it holds, which `resume` reads; a later
approval of the commission's next Suspension replaces it. The capability must be the one the
suspended request needs, as `run` or `resume` named it when it stopped.

Only a stop line `stopped: ApprovalRequired (<action>)` of `run --state` or `resume` leaves a
Suspension to approve. `stopped: ApprovalRequired (<action>), nothing suspended` leaves none, and
`stopped: MergeHandedOff (<request>, HEAD <sha>)` says that HEAD was already handed off: a merge the
agent proposed again at it holds no Suspension, so approving it is refused NothingSuspended, and only
new work, a new HEAD, is approved again.

With --mandate FILE (loom.authority.MandateHost, a host-trusted JSON file), approval also records a
Mandate approval of the request in the state directory's approval log (mandate-approvals.jsonl): the
file's approver approves the capability on the case for the file's verified subject, expiring
approval_seconds later; the approver is neither the verified subject nor its actor. The grant names
it (mandate_approval), and only `resume --mandate` clears it: `resume` without --mandate refuses it.

Exit status:
  0   the grant is written
  10  NothingSuspended: the commission holds no Suspension
  11  InDoubt: the commission's Suspension is being resumed, so its request may have been performed
  19  OtherCapability: the suspended request needs another capability than the one given
  23  AlreadyHandedOff: the suspended repository.merge would hand off a HEAD the commission already handed off
  1   the state directory or the Mandate file cannot be used, or Mandate recorded no approval
  2   the command line is not valid
```

## `b10x-loom resume`

Continue a commission's suspended run after its approval: perform the suspended request once, release the Suspension, and run on until the run stops

```text
Usage: b10x-loom resume [OPTIONS] --state <DIR> <COMMISSION>
```

| Argument | Required | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `<COMMISSION>` | yes | none | The commission whose suspended run is continued |
| `--state <DIR>` | yes | none | The state directory `run --state` kept the commission in, and `approve` wrote its grant into. It must exist; the merge hand-off is recorded there |
| `--mandate <FILE>` | no | none | The host-trusted Mandate file (loom.authority.MandateHost): perform the request only when Mandate's check_with_approval clears and consumes the approval the grant names, keeping the consumption in the state directory's approval log first |

```text
The run is rebuilt from the commission's resume context: the same intent, route, workspace (validated
again), test command, step budget, confinement and agent model; the route is used only when the intent,
the protocol catalog and the context policy are still the ones it was accepted for. The workspace's HEAD
is reported to the case first, so a commit made since the Suspension is refused CaseMoved. The grant
`approve` wrote allows only the request the commission's Suspension holds, and only while it is held. A
granted repository.merge is performed as a merge hand-off: a record of the commission, the request, the
workspace and its HEAD (intake.routing.MergeHandoff, merge-<hex of the request id>.json in the state
directory), only at the HEAD the case holds and once per HEAD of a commission. No Git ref moves; merging
happens outside Loom. The request is performed once, the Suspension is released, and the run goes on as
`run` does. The model does not see the steps before the Suspension.

With --mandate FILE (loom.authority.MandateHost), the request is performed only when Mandate's
check_with_approval clears the approval the grant names (`approve --mandate`), for the file's verified
subject, the capability and the case; its consumption is appended to the state directory's approval
log before anything is performed. A grant naming no approval, an expired, consumed or foreign
approval, or any other Mandate refusal is NotGranted, and nothing is performed. Without --mandate, a
grant naming a Mandate approval (`approve --mandate`) is NotGranted and nothing is performed: only
Mandate clears it.

When the resumed run reaches its human gate again, its last line says what is left to approve:
  stopped: ApprovalRequired (<action>)                    a Suspension `approve` can approve
  stopped: ApprovalRequired (<action>), nothing suspended  nothing to approve
  stopped: MergeHandedOff (<request>, HEAD <sha>)          the case is at a HEAD this commission
                                                           already handed off; nothing to approve

Exit status:
  0   the resumed run reached its human gate again (ApprovalRequired, or MergeHandedOff)
  4   the resumed run reached its human gate holding no Suspension (ApprovalRequired, nothing suspended)
  3   the resumed run stopped for another reason (NothingAdmissible, StepBudget, NoLocalExecutor, ConfinementUnavailable)
  10  NothingSuspended: the commission holds no Suspension, or another resume took and released it first
  11  InDoubt: a resume took the Suspension and did not release it; its request is never performed again
  12  OtherRequest: the Suspension is now held for another request than the one revalidated
  13  OtherCommission: the Suspension or its run names another commission, case or run revision
  14  CaseMoved: the case is no longer at the revision the request was suspended at
  15  NotAdmitted: the current frontier refuses the request's action
  16  NotGranted: no grant allows the request, the grant names a Mandate approval and --mandate is
      not given, or with --mandate Mandate did not clear its approval
  17  NotPerformed: nothing performs the request's action
  18  RunNotSuspended: the run store does not hold the run suspended
  20  the suspension store could not be read; nothing was resumed
  21  the governor could not answer before the run resumed; nothing was resumed
  22  the run could not be resumed, the Suspension could not be taken or released, or the resumed
      loop stopped without a run outcome
  1   anything else failed: the state directory, the resume context, the workspace, the models
  2   the command line is not valid
Nothing is performed on any status from 10 to 21.
```
